settings.question: What is a DTF transfer?
settings.answer: A direct-to-film transfer is your artwork printed onto film and heat-applied to fabric. It gives vivid full-color detail with a soft, flexible finish and strong wash durability.

settings.question: Is there a minimum order?
settings.answer: No minimum, ever. Order a single transfer or thousands - the price per square inch stays the same, and volume discounts kick in automatically as your order grows.

settings.question: What equipment do I need?
settings.answer: A heat press gives the most consistent results, but a household iron or a Cricut EasyPress works too. You need steady heat, even pressure, and about 15 seconds.

settings.question: How long do transfers last?
settings.answer: Our transfers are lab-tested past 100 wash cycles without cracking, peeling, or fading. Wash inside out in cold water to get the most life out of them.

settings.question: What file format should I upload?
settings.answer: PNG with a transparent background at 300 DPI is ideal. We also accept PDF, AI, SVG, TIFF, and JPG. If a file is not print-ready, our art team cleans it up free of charge.

settings.question: How fast is production?
settings.answer: Most orders are printed and shipped within 24 hours. Order before the daily cutoff and your transfers leave the building the next business day.

settings.question: What payment methods do you accept?
settings.answer: All major credit cards, PayPal, Shop Pay, Apple Pay, and Google Pay. Every transaction is encrypted and processed securely at checkout.

settings.question: Do you ship internationally?
settings.answer: Yes, we ship worldwide. Shipping is free on qualifying US orders. International rates and delivery windows vary by destination and are calculated at checkout.

settings.question: Can I put multiple designs on one sheet?
settings.answer: That is exactly what a gang sheet is for. Use the Gang Sheet Builder to arrange as many designs as you can fit, and you only pay for the sheet space you use.

settings.question: How do I track my order?
settings.answer: You will get a tracking number by email as soon as your order ships, and you can follow it in real time from your account or the carrier's site.

settings.heading: DTF Transfers — Single Prints & Bulk Gang Sheets, Any Quantity
settings.description: Our production floor runs a fleet of industry-leading DTF printers, so we handle orders of any size with 24-hour turnaround. From a one-off tee to thousands of gang sheets, every transfer comes off the line with the same color accuracy and wash durability.

settings.label: Print Process
settings.question: How do DTF transfers work?
settings.answer: Your artwork is printed onto a PET film with pigment ink, backed with a hot-melt adhesive powder, and cured. You lay the film on your garment, press it, and peel. No weeding, no cutting, no screens - the design bonds straight into the fabric with a soft, flexible finish.

settings.label: Types
settings.question: What types of transfers can I order?
settings.answer: Standard DTF for everyday apparel, gang sheets to fit many designs on one sheet, UV DTF for mugs and hard surfaces, puff for a raised 3D effect, glitter and metallic foil for decorative accents, reflective for high-visibility workwear, and sublimation for a dye-in-the-fabric hand feel on polyester.

settings.label: Uses
settings.question: What are DTF transfers used for?
settings.answer: Team and event merch, company uniforms and workwear, small-batch clothing brands, school and club apparel, promotional giveaways, and craft or Etsy shops. Because they press onto almost anything, one order can cover tees, hoodies, hats, tote bags, and aprons at once.

settings.label: Materials
settings.question: What fabrics do DTF transfers work on?
settings.answer: Cotton, polyester, cotton-poly blends, tri-blends, canvas, denim, nylon, leather, and most performance fabrics. Light or dark garments both work because every transfer is printed with a white ink underbase, so colors stay accurate on black just as they do on white.

settings.label: Pressing
settings.question: What settings should I press at?
settings.answer: Most transfers press at 300-320°F for 10-15 seconds with medium pressure, then peel. Whether you peel hot or cold depends on the transfer type - the exact setting ships with every order, and full guidance lives on our pressing instructions page.
